messages:
Maya P.: Quick sync — we need a decision on what to push in the next micro-iteration after the launch. Bugs vs enhancements backlog is overflowing, and a few customers asked for UX tweaks. Can we align on priority and rollout plan?
Alex R.: +1. My infra team is free for a hotfix if we mark it P0/P1. Which bugs are we treating as P0?
Maya P.: @Alex R. P0 = crash/data-loss or blocking revenue. I think only one qualifies (indexer crash on long prompts). Everything else is P1 or enhancements.
Tom L.: For enhancements, we should apply a 2-axis filter: Customer impact x dev effort. High impact / low effort = must-do. Medium impact / high effort => backlog.
Priya D.: Agree. Also consider identity of requesting customer (contracted SLA vs public user). For SLA customers, escalate.
Juno CS: FYI a major client raised the streaming consistency issue as a blocker for their rollout. Ticket #4256 — says outputs truncate intermittently. They marked it as blocking.
Maya P.: Ok — let's treat #4256 as P0 for the iteration if Engineering confirms reproducible steps. @Tom L. can you triage?
Tom L.: I can take #4256. I'll try to reproduce this morning and update the ticket with repro steps and a quick mitigation. If reproducible, will target a patch.
Alex R.: If we patch, we should do a canary in prod for the customer region first. Plan: patch -> canary (1% traffic for 1 hour) -> ramp to 20% -> full. Rollback plan included.
triage-bot: Ticket #4256 status changed to "investigating" by Tom L.
Maya P.: Good. For enhancements, I'm proposing we cut two low-value UI polish items from the next slice: floating label tweak and color micro-contrast. Defer to next wave. Keep only the top 3: (1) structured output schema support (customer ask), (2) improved batch caching visibility, (3) faster cold-start path.
Priya D.: Structured output schema support is high impact for the onboarding customers. I can scope a lightweight UX that ships in 1 sprint if we limit to JSON schema + example.
Tom L.: Batch caching visibility: medium effort — needs traces + console bits. Could be half-sprinted with a small backend change and dashboard update.
Alex R.: Faster cold-start path will need runtime tweaks and a small infra budget for warmers. We may need Dedicated commit for predictable gains, otherwise risk cost.
Maya P.: Decision proposal: 1) Hotfix P0s: indexer crash (existing) + streaming truncation (#4256) => immediate fix. 2) Ship structured output schema + batch-caching visibility as the two follow-on enhancements in this micro-iteration. 3) Defer micro-UI polish and cold-start platform work to next cycle unless a significant customer pull emerges.
Juno CS: +1 from CS — we'll update impacted customer SLAs and communicate expected ETA if fixes land within the week.
Tom L.: I'll open a short epic and split into two tickets: one for streaming fix (patch + canary) and one for indexer root-cause. Assigning to me and Alex.
Alex R.: I'll own the canary rollout and rollback playbook. Will add the `canary-checklist.md` link to the tickets.
Maya P.: Action items: (1) Tom: repro + tickets (#4256 + indexer). (2) Alex: canary playbook + infra signoff. (3) Priya: narrow UX scope + example schema. (4) Juno: prepare customer comms draft. Please update Jira labels: iteration=micro-1, priority=P0/P1, impact=customer-facing/high-medium-low.
Tom L.: Will update tickets by EOD and ping once I have repro.
Priya D.: Will drop a wireframe in Figma by tomorrow noon.
Juno CS: I'll draft the comms and run it by Maya before sending.
Maya P.: Thanks. We'll reconvene tomorrow 11am if there are blockers. If any P0 emerges before that please page @oncall. :thumbsup:
triage-bot: Reminder set for 2026-03-22 11:00 UTC (follow-up sync).
